c01.spoken: Next stop: Library Town! Passport out. Stamped.

c02.display: This is stop number 2 of seven. Last time we followed our prompt all the way to an answer. Today we ask where the model came from.
c02.spoken: This is stop number 2 of seven. Last time we followed our prompt all the way to an answer. Today we ask where the model came from.

c03.display: Before it could answer you, the model read a huge share of the public internet: books, articles, websites, code.
c03.spoken: Before it could answer you, the model read a huge share of the public internet: books, articles, websites, code.

c04.display: But here's the twist. All that reading only turned it into a strange autocomplete, not a helpful assistant. Let's see how it went to school.
c04.spoken: But here's the twist. All that reading only turned it into a strange autocomplete, not a helpful assistant. Let's see how it went to school.

c05.display: On the route map, we've left the Departure Gate, and we're here, in Library Town, where the model was trained.
c05.spoken: On the route map, we've left the Departure Gate, and we're here, in Library Town, where the model was trained.

c06.display: Think of the model's training as three stages of school.
c06.spoken: Think of the model's training as three stages of school.

c07.display: Reading: first, it reads an enormous amount of text. This is called pre-training.
c07.spoken: Reading: first, it reads an enormous amount of text. This is called pre-training.

c08.display: Practice: then it practises answering instructions, from worked examples. This is called instruction tuning.
c08.spoken: Practice: then it practises answering instructions, from worked examples. This is called instruction tuning.

c09.display: Feedback: finally, it learns which of its answers people actually prefer.
c09.spoken: Feedback: finally, it learns which of its answers people actually prefer.

c10.display: Stage one, reading. Pre-training means reading a huge amount of text while playing just one game, over and over: predict the next word.
c10.spoken: Stage one, reading. Pre-training means reading a huge amount of text while playing just one game, over and over: predict the next word.

c11.display: Shown "The capital of France is", it learns to predict "Paris". Repeat that across trillions of words, and it picks up grammar, facts, and styles of writing along the way.
c11.spoken: Shown "The capital of France is", it learns to predict "Paris". Repeat that across trillions of words, and it picks up grammar, facts, and styles of writing along the way.

c12.display: Think of a student who reads every book in the library, cover to cover.
c12.spoken: Think of a student who reads every book in the library, cover to cover.

c13.display: So what does the model keep from all that reading? Not what you might expect.
c13.spoken: So what does the model keep from all that reading? Not what you might expect.

c14.display: It doesn't keep a copy of the internet. There's no folder of saved web pages, and it can't look up a page it once read.
c14.spoken: It doesn't keep a copy of the internet. There's no folder of saved web pages, and it can't look up a page it once read.

c15.display: Instead, it keeps patterns, stored in billions of numbers called parameters, which were adjusted a tiny bit with every prediction. Patterns of grammar, facts, styles, and ways of reasoning. Patterns, not pages.
c15.spoken: Instead, it keeps patterns, stored in billions of numbers called parameters, which were adjusted a tiny bit with every prediction. Patterns of grammar, facts, styles, and ways of reasoning. Patterns, not pages.

c16.display: Here's what that strange autocomplete looks like. A model straight out of pre-training is called a base model. Watch what happens when you ask it a question.
c16.spoken: Here's what that strange autocomplete looks like. A model straight out of pre-training is called a base model. Watch what happens when you ask it a question.

c17.display: You type: "What is the capital of France?"
c17.spoken: You type: "What is the capital of France?"

c18.display: And it might reply: "What is the capital of Germany? What is the capital of Italy?" It isn't being rude. It's continuing the text, the way a list of quiz questions continues online.
c18.spoken: And it might reply: "What is the capital of Germany? What is the capital of Italy?" It isn't being rude. It's continuing the text, the way a list of quiz questions continues online.

c19.display: Stage two, practice. Instruction tuning means more training on many examples of instructions paired with good answers, so the model learns to respond like an assistant.
c19.spoken: Stage two, practice. Instruction tuning means more training on many examples of instructions paired with good answers, so the model learns to respond like an assistant.

c20.display: For example: "Summarise this article", followed by a clear, short summary. Thousands of examples like that teach it the shape of a helpful reply.
c20.spoken: For example: "Summarise this article", followed by a clear, short summary. Thousands of examples like that teach it the shape of a helpful reply.

c21.display: It's like practising past exam papers, with model answers to learn from.
c21.spoken: It's like practising past exam papers, with model answers to learn from.

c22.display: Stage three, feedback. Often called reinforcement learning from human feedback, or RLHF. It works like this.
c22.spoken: Stage three, feedback. Often called reinforcement learning from human feedback, or R L H F. It works like this.

c23.display: Generate: the model writes two different answers to the same prompt.
c23.spoken: Generate: the model writes two different answers to the same prompt.

c24.display: Compare: people look at both, and pick the better one.
c24.spoken: Compare: people look at both, and pick the better one.

c25.display: Learn: from many of those choices, a separate scoring model learns what people tend to prefer.
c25.spoken: Learn: from many of those choices, a separate scoring model learns what people tend to prefer.

c26.display: Improve: the main model is then tuned to write answers that score higher. That's where much of its politeness and helpfulness comes from.
c26.spoken: Improve: the main model is then tuned to write answers that score higher. That's where much of its politeness and helpfulness comes from.

c27.display: There's one catch to all this schooling, and it explains a lot of confusing answers.
c27.spoken: There's one catch to all this schooling, and it explains a lot of confusing answers.

c28.display: The model's reading stops at a certain date, called its knowledge cutoff.
c28.spoken: The model's reading stops at a certain date, called its knowledge cutoff.

c29.display: Anything that happened after that was never in its library, so it simply doesn't know about it.
c29.spoken: Anything that happened after that was never in its library, so it simply doesn't know about it.

c30.display: Unless the app around it adds a web search, and passes the results in with your question.
c30.spoken: Unless the app around it adds a web search, and passes the results in with your question.

c31.display: Time for "Try it yourself". Grab your phone.
c31.spoken: Time for "Try it yourself". Grab your phone.

c32.display: First, with web search turned off, ask a chatbot: "What happened in the news last week?"
c32.spoken: First, with web search turned off, ask a chatbot: "What happened in the news last week?"

c33.display: Then turn search on, and ask again. Compare the two answers. Notice which one admits it doesn't know, and which one can actually tell you.
c33.spoken: Then turn search on, and ask again. Compare the two answers. Notice which one admits it doesn't know, and which one can actually tell you.

c35.display: The myth: the model learns from my chats in real time.
c35.spoken: The myth: the model learns from my chats in real time.

c36.display: The reality: its knowledge is fixed when training ends. Within a conversation it can use what you've said, like short-term memory, but that doesn't change the model itself. Whether conversations are used to train future versions depends on the app and your settings.
c36.spoken: The reality: its knowledge is fixed when training ends. Within a conversation it can use what you've said, like short-term memory, but that doesn't change the model itself. Whether conversations are used to train future versions depends on the app and your settings.

c37.display: And here's your "Use it tomorrow" tip: don't trust recent facts unless search is on.
c37.spoken: And here's your "Use it tomorrow" tip: don't trust recent facts unless search is on.

c38.display: If you're asking about anything recent, turn search on. Ask for sources and dates. And double-check anything that changes fast, like prices, laws, or the news.
c38.spoken: If you're asking about anything recent, turn search on. Ask for sources and dates. And double-check anything that changes fast, like prices, laws, or the news.

c39.display: Let's stamp the passport. The model went to school in three stages: reading, practice, and feedback.
c39.spoken: Let's stamp the passport. The model went to school in three stages: reading, practice, and feedback.

c40.display: It stores patterns, not pages, and its knowledge stops at a cutoff date.
c40.spoken: It stores patterns, not pages, and its knowledge stops at a cutoff date.
